summary: A first-person narrator (Marcus) walks with a girl named Ange after school, sharing a passage from a book that praises 'mad' people who burn with life, and feels happy. Their walk is interrupted when Van, a former close friend, appears. Van seems shaken, and Marcus is embarrassed to be seen with Ange. Marcus explains to Ange that he and Van were once best friends in an ARG with Jose-Luis and Darryl, and that they were all arrested together, but Van stopped being friends after disliking the Xnet, fearing Marcus would get others in trouble.
one_line: Marcus meets his former friend Van after school while walking with Ange, and explains their falling out over the Xnet and an earlier arrest.
key_facts: The narrator shares a passage from a book with Ange describing 'dingledodies' and people who are 'mad to live, mad to talk, mad to be saved'.
The passage describes mad people who 'burn, burn, burn like fabulous yellow roman candles exploding like spiders across the stars'.
Ange puts her arm around the narrator's waist as they walk down the street toward the bus-stop.
The narrator suppresses the urge to take his arm off Ange's shoulders when Van appears.
Van is described as seeming surprised, not angry, and 'more ashen, shaken' when she sees the narrator with Ange.
The narrator says he hadn't spoken to Van in weeks, and that those weeks felt like months.
Van, Jose-Luis and Darryl were with the narrator when they were arrested.
The narrator, Van, Jose-Luis and Darryl used to play an ARG together and were kind of best friends.
The narrator says Van 'didn't like the Xnet' and thought they would get into trouble.
The narrator says Van thought he would get other people into trouble.
The narrator notices many girls from the school behind them but no Van when he looks over his shoulder.
